entry.title: Oxide Computer Company Secures $445M Series D Funding Round (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Who's building on-prem compute in 2026? It turns out a lot of people! Oxide Computer Company, which builds custom on-prem cloud compute systems, has closed a massive $445 million Series D funding round led by Eclipse, with participation from major investors including Jane Street, Atreides Management, and chipmaker AMD. The capital injection follows the startup achieving operational profitability and will be used to scale manufacturing capacity, secure raw material inventory, and fulfill a rapidly expanding order backlog for their commercial cloud computer racks.

entry.title: SpaceX buys 800 MHz low-band spectrum to pair terrestrial towers with 2 GHz Starlink satellites (3 minute read)
entry.content:
SpaceX agreed to buy up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz low-band spectrum, which penetrates buildings, and plans to deploy its own antennas on towers and rooftops to use it, with most existing phones already supporting the band. Separately, the FCC approved 15,000 more Starlink satellites optimized for 2 GHz. Together they point to a hybrid network, terrestrial indoors and satellite beyond towers. The deal needs FCC approval, and Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile shares fell roughly 6% on the news.

entry.title: The Machines That Make the Machines: Advancing Industrial Digital Twins (5 minute read)
entry.content:
In this rare peek under the hood, we get a glimpse of how Foxconn uses NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac, and Metropolis platforms to create physically accurate digital twins of manufacturing facilities that assemble next-generation AI server hardware. By simulating factory layouts, automated optical inspection systems, and autonomous mobile robot fleets in virtual environments before physical deployment, the company minimizes factory commissioning delays and boosts production efficiency. This approach showcases how system architects and automation specialists can leverage high-fidelity simulation to safely validate and optimize complex robotic workcells prior to hardware installation.

entry.title: Blue Origin rebuilds LC-36 for vertical New Glenn integration, targeting a December return (4 minute read)
entry.content:
After May's pad explosion destroyed its transporter-erector, Blue Origin is rebuilding LC-36 for vertical integration, loading New Glenn through the support tower alone, as with Starship. Crews destacked the tower, added cryogenic propellant plumbing on the ground, and have begun restacking modules, while the launch bridge is restored. Umbilicals and fairing access platforms haven't appeared yet. Bezos targets a December return to flight carrying Blue Ring, though he joked it could slip to December 31.

entry.title: Photonic chips learn after fabrication by measuring their own optical gradients (3 minute read)
entry.content:
A Nature Computational Science briefing describes an in situ learning method where photonic integrated circuits directly measure optical gradients, so diverse circuit layouts can be trained after they're built. That removes the need for a full digital model of the chip, which optical training normally leans on. The team demonstrated matrix design, multiwavelength computation, and rapid meta-learning on the hardware. Specifics like accuracy or energy figures aren't included.

entry.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM (2 minute read)
entry.content:
ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction from the Oxford Robot Dynamics Lab. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability

entry.title: Amazon builds its 1,000th Leo satellite at 27 a week, but only 396 are in orbit (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Amazon built its 1,000th Leo broadband satellite at its Kirkland, Washington plant, which took six months to produce its first 27 and now turns out 27 a week. It builds propulsion in-house and borrowed consumer electronics methods to cut tests that took weeks down to hours. The bottleneck is launch: only 396 are in orbit against 3,232 needed, and the Vulcan grounding and a New Glenn pad explosion cost Amazon FCC spectrum priority.

entry.title: Anderon aims to industrialize quantum chip fabrication (5 minute read)
entry.content:
IEEE Spectrum examines the up-to-$1B CHIPS R&D award finalized for IBM spinoff Anderon in September. IBM is matching that funding with $1B, while Anderon uses a 300mm Albany line and plans foundry services and process design kits for outside developers. The challenge is repeatable fabrication, including tighter control of Josephson junctions, rather than simply adding wafer capacity.

entry.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, a GPU engine that runs one shader set across OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and OpenGL ES (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Tensor virtualization decouples a tensor's logical layout from its physical GPU allocation, so one shader template replaces separate backend-specific codebases. For edge LLMs, ML Drift switches kernels between compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode, using a convolution-aligned KV cache layout and in-kernel activation quantization to skip memory roundtrips. It cut YouTube Shorts frame latency by up to 40%, and Google co-optimized it with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs.

entry.title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Gartner predicts that over half of quantum startups will fail by 2030 due to a market unable to generate sufficient revenue. Despite this, companies are investing in quantum technologies for their potential business advantages, focusing on building expertise rather than waiting for technological maturity. The public sector and financial industries are expected to lead quantum computing investments, with spending reaching $245 million and $289 million by 2027 and 2028, respectively.

entry.title: SpaceX seeks $40B Apollo-led debt financing to buy Nvidia chips (2 minute read)
entry.content:
The FT reports SpaceX is raising about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt to fund an Nvidia chip order, with Apollo leading and helping sell the debt to a broad investor base, and bond fund Pimco among lenders in talks. The deal is expected to close in 2027. It fits the pattern Nvidia flagged in August, when it disclosed its own SpaceX stake and a $500 billion Wall Street financing push, with chip purchases increasingly funded by debt and equity ties to the buyer. Reuters could not independently verify the report, and SpaceX, Apollo, Nvidia, and Pimco haven't commented.

entry.title: Synopsys and OpenAI team up on GPT-Synopsys, a frontier model that runs EDA tools like an engineer (4 minute read)
entry.content:
GPT-Synopsys is an OpenAI frontier model trained and tuned to operate Synopsys' EDA tools directly, covering PPA optimization, timing closure, and verification. Engineers hand it an objective, and agents run the tools, interpret the results, make changes, and loop until there's a verified outcome to review. It runs on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and plugs into Synopsys.ai and the Autopilot agentic platform. OpenAI licenses Synopsys' tools to train the model, paying a training subscription fee, and the two companies then share revenue based on how well the model improves chip designs, an unusual structure that ties both to the results. Synopsys says customer design data stays protected and won't be used to train the frontier model, and the bundled service covers compute, the model, and EDA licenses.

entry.title: OpenTPU Full-Stack Open-Source AI Accelerator (2 minute read)
entry.content:
OpenTPU is a complete, open-source AI accelerator project that packages custom SystemVerilog RTL, instruction set architecture, a bit-exact simulator, and a compiler into a single accessible repository. The design runs modern quantized language models directly on cost-effective Kintex-7 FPGA PCIe cards, matching simulation results bit for bit. This architecture provides embedded systems designers and compute engineers an invaluable end-to-end reference for deploying and tailoring custom neural network hardware without relying on proprietary black-box tooling.

entry.title: California man charged with smuggling $300M of Nvidia AI servers to China through Malaysia and Singapore (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Federal prosecutors arrested Greg (Yiu Kong) Lui, owner of San Gabriel Valley company Earthmade, on charges of exporting more than $300 million of servers loaded with export-controlled Nvidia AI GPUs to China between 2023 and 2024. The scheme worked by exploiting a licensing gap: Commerce doesn't require an export license to ship this hardware to Malaysia or Singapore, but does for China, so Lui allegedly sent servers to Malaysian and Singapore transshipment companies using false paperwork, then used freight forwarders to move them on to Chinese buyers.

It highlights a major shift toward utilizing integrated foundation models and highly flexible physical platforms to automate complex, multi-step commercial and industrial service roles.

It serves as a prime case study of how custom autonomous technology can successfully transition from controlled, simulated environments into the real-world logistics and shipping infrastructure.

Cowboy Space's Reason-1 tests beaming solar power via laser, Google's Project Suncatcher runs AI chips on solar in orbit to evaluate durability, and Star Catcher's Protostar aims to validate power-beaming to satellites. These tests are crucial for building infrastructure to support future AI computing and data centers in space.

entry.title: Crossing Chiplet Boundaries With PCIe Over UCIe (5 minute read)
entry.content:
PCIe 8.0 traffic can cross chiplet boundaries through UCIe 3.0, but engineers must coordinate both protocols' power, reset, and recovery states. Timing mismatches can cause completion timeouts, dropped traffic, and deadlocks. Siemens' verification tools trace transactions across both layers and inject faults before silicon bring-up.

entry.title: Memory At The Edge: Non-Volatile Memory Challenges And Requirements For Humanoid Robots (8 minute read)
entry.content:
Humanoid robots need different memory architectures for centralized AI compute and distributed joint control. Flash and EEPROM can delay writes by 5-10 milliseconds, which risks lost position data during power failures. The article maps F-RAM to continuous telemetry, safety-capable NOR Flash to boot storage, and high-speed NOR Flash to time-sensitive networking.

entry.title: OpenArm 2.0: An Open-Source Compliant Robotic Arm (4 minute read)
entry.content:
OpenArm 2.0 is an open-source, 7-degree-of-freedom robotic arm engineered by Tokyo-based Enactic for contact-rich manipulation and physical artificial intelligence research. The arm features backdrivable, quasi-direct drive joints for highly compliant physical interactions, a gripper with an integrated camera, and a motorless replica arm for bilateral force-feedback teleoperation. It delivers a highly customizable, low-cost platform that facilitates the training of robust manipulation models using modern imitation learning and simulation-to-reality pipelines.

It provides a complete, open-source blueprint for constructing complex, dynamically stable legged systems using advanced embedded processors and modern spatial computing toolchains.
